### `computePivotState`

Compute initial collapsed + swapped sets that pivot the tree to display
`identifier` at the top with everything else collapsed.

Resolution order:
  1. A leaf whose `geneId` matches `identifier`.
  2. A node whose `id` matches `identifier`.
  3. Otherwise null (with a console warning).

The pivot:
- Every internal node that is NOT on the root-to-target path is added
  to `collapsedNodeIds` (turning the deepest possible visible
  ancestors into triangles). Uncollapsing any of those triangles
  reveals the next level — also triangles — so the user can drill
  down level by level. Leaves are never collapsed (they're already
  minimal). The target's own descendants are also collapsed for the
  same drill-down reason.
- For each ancestor whose path-child is not its first child,
  `swappedNodeIds` includes the ancestor so its children render in
  reversed order, putting the path-child on top. (Assumes binary
  ancestors; for non-binary trees this is a best-effort pivot.)

```ts
function computePivotState(tree: Tree, identifier: string): PivotState | null;
```

### `fromHierarchy`

Flatten a nested node structure into a tbrowse `Tree` (+ `Taxonomy`) by
a pre-order walk. Node ids are `String(acc.id(n))`; a node whose id was
already seen is skipped together with its subtree (and reported in
`warnings`), so a malformed, cyclic or duplicate-id hierarchy cannot spin
the walk. A node is a leaf when it has no children.
Origin: gramene-search `taxTree/toTbrowseTree.js:23-62` (the `walk`),
generalised over accessor functions.

```ts
function fromHierarchy<N>(root: N, acc: HierarchyAccessors<N>): FromHierarchyResult;
```

### `fromTreeModel`

gramene-search's taxonomy-tree adapter: node id = `String(model.id)`,
`distance` 0 for the root and `opts.distance` (default 1) otherwise,
`taxonomyId` = the id (a string by default; `taxonomyIdAs: 'number'`
emits `Number(model.id)`), and a `Taxonomy` entry per node exposing
`model.name` as both `scientificName` and `commonName` (so the labels zone
shows something whichever field is active) plus `rank`. `leafTaxonIds` are
the leaf ids in pre-order, as the TaxDist view consumes them.
Origin: gramene-search `taxTree/toTbrowseTree.js:23-62` (`toTbrowseTree`).

```ts
function fromTreeModel(root: TreeModelLike, opts?: {
    distance?: number;
    taxonomyIdAs?: 'string' | 'number';
}): FromHierarchyResult & {
    leafTaxonIds: string[];
};
```

### `leavesFailing`

Ids of the leaves (in `leafIdsOf` order) that `keepLeaf` rejects —
leaf-only pruning. Hiding just the leaves is enough for a viewer, since
internal nodes with no visible descendants contribute no rows. The
original filtered the adapter's pre-order `leafTaxonIds`; the id set is
identical, and only the order can differ (integer-like ids enumerate
numerically), which `ViewState.prunedNodeIds` ignores.
Origin: gramene-search `TaxDistTbrowse.js:156-167`
(`adapter.leafTaxonIds.filter((id) => !selected[id])`).

```ts
function leavesFailing(tree: Tree, keepLeaf: (leaf: TreeNode) => boolean): NodeId[];
```

### `maximalExcludedClades`

Ids of the highest nodes whose entire subtree contains no leaf that
`keepLeaf` accepts (maximal excluded clades), so a viewer sheds one stub
per clade instead of one per leaf. Lifted filter, kept verbatim: a node is
returned when it keeps nothing AND (it is the root OR its parent keeps
something). Consequently, when NO leaf is kept the result is `[rootId]` —
callers that must never prune the root (Homology keeps the gene of
interest) guarantee that through `keepLeaf`. Nodes whose parent id is not
in `tree.nodes` are treated as keeping nothing.
Origin: gramene-search `details/Homology.js:107-137` (`getGenomePrunedIds`).

```ts
function maximalExcludedClades(tree: Tree, keepLeaf: (leaf: TreeNode) => boolean, childrenIndex?: ChildrenIndex): NodeId[];
```

Node heights for an (approximately) ultrametric tree: `height = maxRootDistance − rootDistance`,

```ts
function nodeHeights(tree: Tree, childrenIndex?: ChildrenIndex): {
```

### `postorder`

Node ids in post-order (children before their parent), honouring swaps.
Same skipping rules as `preorder`; iterative.

```ts
function postorder(tree: Tree, opts?: WalkOptions): NodeId[];
```

### `preorder`

Node ids in pre-order (a node before its children), honouring swaps. The
walk is iterative so deep (caterpillar) trees cannot overflow the stack;
ids that are missing from `tree.nodes` are skipped, and the children of a
node flagged `isLeaf` are never visited.

```ts
function preorder(tree: Tree, opts?: WalkOptions): NodeId[];
```

### `pruneToLeaves`

Prune a tree to the leaves in `keep` (a set of leaf ids or a predicate).
Internal nodes with no surviving descendant are dropped; with
`collapseUnary` (default) an internal node left with one surviving child
is spliced out and the child's branch length becomes the sum of the two,
so root-to-leaf distances are preserved. When the root itself is spliced
the surviving child becomes the new root (its `parentId` is nulled; its
summed `distance` is kept). Returns null when no leaf survives. Node
insertion order — and therefore child order — is preserved.
Origin: gramene-g2p `apps/ui/src/pages/Genotypes.tsx:530-538`
(`pruneToSamples`, binary `L ?? R` collapse), generalised to n-ary trees.

```ts
function pruneToLeaves(tree: Tree, keep: ReadonlySet<NodeId> | ((leaf: TreeNode) => boolean), opts?: PruneOptions): Tree | null;
```

### `quoteNewickLabel`

Quote a Newick label when it contains whitespace or Newick punctuation
(`,():;'[]`), doubling embedded single quotes; otherwise return it as is.
Origin: gramene-g2p `apps/api/src/cluster.ts:109-112` (`quote`).

```ts
function quoteNewickLabel(label: string): string;
```

### `rollUp`

Generic post-order aggregation: every leaf reachable from the root gets
`leafValue(leaf)`, every internal node gets `combine(childValues, node)`
where `childValues` are its children's results in child order. Nodes not
reachable from the root are absent from the result; a child id missing
from `tree.nodes` contributes nothing. Iterative, so deep trees are safe.

`sumLeafCounts`, `countsFromFacet`, `sumByNode` and `maxByNode` are all
instances of this.

```ts
function rollUp<T>(tree: Tree, leafValue: (leaf: TreeNode) => T, combine: (childValues: T[], node: TreeNode) => T, opts?: {
    childrenIndex?: ChildrenIndex;
}): Record<NodeId, T>;
```

### `subtree`

The subtree rooted at `rootId` as a standalone tree: the same node
objects (shallow-copied) in their original insertion order, with the new
root's `parentId` set to null and its `distance` kept. Throws when
`rootId` is not in the tree.

```ts
function subtree(tree: Tree, rootId: NodeId): Tree;
```

### `subtreeIdsOf`

All node ids in the subtree rooted at `rootId`, including `rootId` itself.

```ts
function subtreeIdsOf(rootId: NodeId, childrenIndex: ChildrenIndex): Set<NodeId>;
```

### `sumLeafCounts`

Sum per-leaf counts up the tree so every node (not just leaves) has a
total: a leaf's count is `leafCounts[id] || 0`, an internal node's is the
sum over its children — what a collapsed-summary row should display.
Origin: gramene-search `taxTree/countsZone.js:20-53` (`computeGeneCounts`,
minus the facet parsing, which lives in `zone/counts.ts`).

```ts
function sumLeafCounts(tree: Tree, leafCounts: Record<NodeId, number>): Record<NodeId, number>;
```

### `swapsForLeafOrder`

Compute the `ViewState.swappedNodeIds` that make `leafOrder(tree, …)`
reproduce a requested leaf `order` (labels compared via `key(leaf)`,
default `geneId ?? id`). Each internal node is flagged when the minimum
requested rank among its children's subtrees runs strictly downward in
child order, so reversing it sorts them; for binary trees any order the
topology can realise is reproduced exactly, for polytomies only
reversals are available. Leaves absent from `order` rank last and never
cause a swap; labels in `order` matching no leaf are listed in
`unmatched`. This is how a BrAPI `tree.leafOrder` or g2p's `leafOrder()`
is mapped back onto a viewer view state.

```ts
function swapsForLeafOrder(tree: Tree, order: readonly string[], key?: (leaf: TreeNode) => string): {
    swappedNodeIds: NodeId[];
    unmatched: string[];
};
```

### `toNewick`

Newick serialisation of a tree (or of the subtree under `rootId`): children
in child order (`opts.childrenIndex`, default the enumeration order of
`tree.nodes` — see `buildChildrenIndex` for the numeric-id caveat;
reversed for `swappedNodeIds`), `:length` from each node's `distance`
formatted with `toFixed(precision)`, no length on the root, trailing `;`.
With the defaults this reproduces gramene-g2p's `toNewick` byte for byte
on its binary UPGMA trees, where `distance = parent.height − child.height`
and node ids are synthetic (so sample names never affect child order).
Origin: gramene-g2p `apps/api/src/cluster.ts:99-107` (`toNewick`).

```ts
function toNewick(tree: Tree, opts?: ToNewickOptions): string;
```

### `validateTree`

Structural problems with a tree, as human-readable strings; `[]` when
the tree is sound. Checks: the root exists and has no parent, every
`parentId` names a node, at least one leaf, no cycles, every node is
reachable from the root, and `isLeaf` agrees with having no children.

```ts
function validateTree(tree: Tree): string[];
```

## Interfaces

### `FromHierarchyResult`

Result of flattening a hierarchy. `leafIds` are in pre-order (display) order.

```ts
interface FromHierarchyResult {
    tree: Tree;
    taxonomy: Taxonomy;
    leafIds: NodeId[];
    warnings: string[];
}
```

### `HierarchyAccessors`

How to read a nested (hierarchical) node type `N` when flattening it into
a `Tree`. Only `id` and `children` are required; the rest are optional
decorations. `distance` defaults to 0 for the root and 1 otherwise (a
uniform cladogram, as a taxonomy carries no branch lengths).

```ts
interface HierarchyAccessors<N> {
    id: (n: N) => string | number;
    children: (n: N) => readonly N[] | undefined;
    distance?: (n: N, parent: N | null) => number;
    taxonomyId?: (n: N) => TaxonomyId | undefined;
    geneId?: (n: N) => GeneId | undefined;
    /** Taxonomy entry to record under `String(taxonomyId(n))`. */
    taxon?: (n: N) => TaxonomyNode | undefined;
}
```

### `PivotState`

```ts
interface PivotState {
    collapsedNodeIds: NodeId[];
    swappedNodeIds: NodeId[];
    /** The resolved id of the target node (leaf gene id match takes precedence). */
    targetId: NodeId;
}
```

### `PruneOptions`

Options for `pruneToLeaves`.

```ts
interface PruneOptions {
    /**
     * Splice internal nodes left with a single surviving child, adding the
     * spliced node's `distance` onto the child's (default true). With false,
     * unary internal nodes are kept.
     */
    collapseUnary?: boolean;
}
```

### `ToNewickOptions`

Options for `toNewick`.

```ts
interface ToNewickOptions {
    /**
     * Label for a node, or null for none. Default: leaves are labelled with
     * `geneId ?? id`, internal nodes carry no label (matching gramene-g2p's
     * serialiser).
     */
    label?: (node: TreeNode) => string | null;
    /** Emit `:length` after every non-root node (default true). */
    branchLengths?: boolean;
    /** Decimal places for branch lengths via `toFixed` (default 6). */
    precision?: number;
    /** Serialise only the subtree under this node (default: the tree root). */
    rootId?: NodeId;
    /** Internal nodes whose children are written in reversed order. */
    swappedNodeIds?: ReadonlySet<NodeId>;
    /**
     * Explicit child order. Default: `buildChildrenIndex(tree)`, i.e. the
     * enumeration order of `tree.nodes` — which puts canonical-integer ids
     * first in numeric order. Pass an index built from an ordered source
     * when node ids are numeric strings and insertion order matters.
     */
    childrenIndex?: ChildrenIndex;
}
```

### `TreeModelLike`

The shape of a gramene `taxonomy-with-genomes` tree node (and of any
`tree-model` node): `model.id` is the NCBI taxon id, `model.name` the
display name, `model.rank` the rank; `children` the subclades.

```ts
interface TreeModelLike {
    model: {
        id: string | number;
        name?: string;
        rank?: string;
    };
    children?: TreeModelLike[];
}
```

### `WalkOptions`

Options shared by the traversal helpers. `rootId` restricts the walk to a
subtree (default: the tree root); `swappedNodeIds` is the viewer's
`ViewState.swappedNodeIds` as a set — an internal node listed there has
its children visited in reversed order, so the walk yields display order;
`childrenIndex` lets callers reuse a precomputed `buildChildrenIndex`, or
supply an explicitly ordered one (numeric node ids otherwise enumerate
first, in numeric order — see `buildChildrenIndex`).

```ts
interface WalkOptions {
    rootId?: NodeId;
    swappedNodeIds?: ReadonlySet<NodeId>;
    childrenIndex?: ChildrenIndex;
}
```

## Type aliases

### `ChildrenIndex`

Children index for a tree, keyed by parent id. Child order is the
enumeration order of `Object.keys(tree.nodes)`: insertion order, EXCEPT
that canonical-integer keys (`'3'`, `'12'`) always enumerate first, in
ascending numeric order — a JavaScript object invariant, and the same
order the viewer walks (`computeVisibleRows`). Trees whose node ids are
numeric strings therefore lose insertion order; give such trees
synthetic ids (the parsers and the UPGMA builder do) or pass an
explicitly ordered `ChildrenIndex` to the walks and to `toNewick`.

```ts
type ChildrenIndex = ReadonlyMap<NodeId, readonly NodeId[]>;
```
